task.description: Rework 3 of 3 (final in budget) for ISS-0427 design, per ELIXIR-DEV's BLOCKER at Step 3 implementation (handoffs/WF03-ISS0427-20260904/step-03-elixir-dev.json). This design's trigger-dormancy premise (repeated across 3 design passes and 2 validator gates) is false: 5 real, security-relevant immutability triggers (audit_entries x2, repository_artifacts x2, artifact_versions x1) exist in priv/repo/migrations/20260830020001 and 20260830030001, confirmed against a real built template. Required: design trigger/trigger-function recreation (same qualifier-rewrite class as the FK fix), fix dimension #8 to a real structural check, re-run every remaining dormancy claim against both migration source and a real template catalog (the coordinator's suspicion: narrow-pattern greps missed this one), and fold in ELIXIR-DEV's four MINOR fixes (advisory-lock connection-boundary bug, missing schema_migrations clone step, ordinal_position false-fail, index-name-string comparison bug).

result.summary:
lib/letflow/design/iss0427-tenant-test-schema-template-clone.md updated in place. New section 0.4 documents the finding, the full re-audit table, and the mechanism/check fixes.

THE BLOCKER, independently re-verified (not inherited from ELIXIR-DEV's report): read both migrations directly (20260830020001_create_audit_entries_tenant_scoped.exs, 20260830030001_create_repository_artifacts.exs) and confirmed the exact 5 triggers / 3 functions ELIXIR-DEV found. Built an equivalent probe (function+2 triggers on a template table), confirmed pg_get_functiondef/pg_get_triggerdef both emit template-schema-qualified text, confirmed a LIKE INCLUDING ALL clone gets zero triggers, then built and verified the fix end-to-end: created the function in the clone schema via pg_get_functiondef with the schema qualifier textually substituted (same technique as the FK rewrite), then the triggers via pg_get_triggerdef with the same substitution -- confirmed the clone's function is a genuinely distinct pg_proc object, confirmed the immutability guarantee fires against the CLONE independently, and -- checked specifically because the DOMAIN/ENUM finding (rework 2) showed a superficially similar mechanism can still leave a live coupling -- confirmed the clone remains fully functional after the TEMPLATE schema is dropped entirely (unlike domains/enums/collations, a function/trigger created via CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION/CREATE TRIGGER in a different schema is, by Postgres construction, a wholly independent object once recreated, not a shared reference). All probe schemas dropped clone-before-template and confirmed gone.

DESIGN FIX 1 -- MECHANISM (section 2.3, new step 6, inserted between sequence recreation and seed-data copy, renumbering subsequent steps): per table, discover triggers via pg_trigger (NOT tgisinternal, explicitly excluding the RI_ConstraintTrigger_* rows FK enforcement creates, which are a side effect of step 4 not this step's concern) joined to pg_proc for the backing function OID; for each DISTINCT function OID, pg_get_functiondef with template-qualifier textually replaced by the clone's, executed as-is; for each trigger, pg_get_triggerdef with the same substitution. Explicit sequencing rule stated (all functions before any trigger, since CREATE TRIGGER resolves its EXECUTE FUNCTION target at creation time) since getting this wrong is a real implementation hazard the design must not leave ambiguous.

DESIGN FIX 2 -- THE CHECK (section 3.2 item 8's triggers sub-bullet, rewritten as a REWORK 3 CORRECTION, not a quiet edit): pg_trigger compared as a per-table multiset of pg_get_triggerdef text (schema-qualifier-normalized) -- this single comparison catches a missing trigger, a differently-defined one, AND (the exact hazard the mechanism fix targets) one that is present but still calls the TEMPLATE's function; a SECOND comparison covers the backing functions themselves via pg_get_functiondef, per-schema multiset, for the same reason dimension #4 (indexes) needed both an existence and a structural check. Stated explicitly that this dimension, unlike #9-11/#13, is immediately load-bearing today (5 real triggers on the reference side), not a defaults-only forward guard.

POINT 3 -- THE FULL RE-AUDIT TABLE (reproduced here, full version in section 0.4): re-ran every remaining dormancy claim as a WIDE, case-insensitive grep against priv/repo/migrations/*.exs (not anchored to any prior pass's exact phrasing), since the root cause of the miss was diagnosed and confirmed: the trigger claim was checked via execute("CREATE TRIGGER" -style anchored patterns, which cannot match the real migrations' actual execute(<heredoc>, <heredoc>) two-argument call shape even when the content was already present -- this was 'too narrow,' exactly the coordinator's suspicion, not 'not run.' Results: Triggers (CREATE TRIGGER) -- FALSE, 5 triggers in 2 files, this section's own finding. Constraint triggers (CREATE CONSTRAINT TRIGGER specifically) -- zero hits, genuinely dormant, unaffected. reloptions/WITH(fillfactor...) -- zero hits; additionally cross-checked all 18 execute() call sites in the tree by reading each one directly (not just grepping), confirmed every one is either the trigger/function finding above, an ADD CONSTRAINT CHECK (already dimension #3), a partial CREATE INDEX WHERE (already dimension #4), or a one-time DO $$ data-migration block with no persistent structural residue -- still dormant. SET STATISTICS -- zero hits, still dormant. CREATE STATISTICS -- zero hits, still dormant. CREATE TYPE/CREATE DOMAIN -- zero hits, still dormant (OQ-6 correctly still deferred). CREATE COLLATION -- zero hits, still dormant (OQ-6 correctly still deferred). COMMENT ON (any kind) -- zero hits, still dormant. ROW LEVEL SECURITY -- zero hits, still dormant. PARTITION BY -- zero hits, still dormant. TABLESPACE -- zero hits, still dormant. Only the trigger claim was false; every other dormancy claim in the document re-confirmed true under the wider method.

CORRECTED THE ROOT-CAUSE STATEMENTS IN PLACE, not just the check: section 0.2 finding 7 and section 3.2 dimension #3's own REWORK NOTE both previously stated 'no migration contains CREATE TRIGGER' as part of explaining why constraint triggers (contype='t') were dormant -- that broader claim was false even though the narrower constraint-trigger-specific claim was and remains true. Both locations corrected in place to state precisely which half was right and which was wrong, rather than leaving a stale, now-contradicted sentence standing next to the new section 0.4 finding.

FOLDED IN ELIXIR-DEV'S FOUR MINOR FIXES, all found true and load-bearing on re-reading the mechanism, not merely narrated: (1) section 4.3's advisory lock corrected from transaction-scoped pg_advisory_xact_lock (does not work -- Ecto.Migrator.run/4 checks out its own connection, invisible to the outer transaction's CREATE SCHEMA, reproducible Postgrex 3F000) to a session-level pg_advisory_lock/pg_advisory_unlock pair with no wrapping transaction, matching SandboxPool.provision_sandbox/2's own established pattern -- scoped to ensure_template!/0 only, clone_tenant_schema!/1 unaffected. (2) section 2.3's schema_migrations step split into an explicit CREATE TABLE (LIKE ... INCLUDING ALL) sub-step before the INSERT ... SELECT, since expected_tenant_tables/0 deliberately excludes schema_migrations so nothing in the per-table LIKE loop was ever going to create it -- the design's prose had assumed it existed. (3) dimension #2 (columns) corrected to compare RELATIVE column rank (re-ranked 1..N) rather than raw ordinal_position, since REQ-064's ten tenant_id-drop migrations leave permanent ordinal gaps in the template that LIKE renumbers away in the clone -- a benign difference the raw comparison would have false-failed on every affected table. (4) noted as an implementation-bug caveat in section 0.4 (ELIXIR-DEV's own bug, not a design defect, so not a design-text correction) that dimension #4/#11's structural comparison must strip the index/statistics-object's own auto-generated name before comparing, not just its ON-clause -- flagging for REVIEWER to specifically re-check per ELIXIR-DEV's own request, since the design's text already specified this correctly and the bug was in a first-pass implementation, not the design.

OQ-2 marked RESOLVED (not deleted) with a note that it was a false premise dressed as a deferred design choice, not a genuine option left open.

Section 11's acceptance-criteria table updated: OQ-1's resolution (option (b), confirmed via ELIXIR-DEV's own step-3 handoff) and a new row for the trigger/trigger-function hazard, parallel to the existing FK and sequence rows.

Everything confirmed sound by the coordinator's own message (FK rewrite, sequence recreation, dimensions 1-7 and 9-13's core specifications, the parity check's proven non-vacuity) was left untouched except where a dimension's OWN text needed the corrections above (dimension #2's ordinal-position fix, dimension #8's full rewrite) -- not re-litigated beyond what the blocker and its four MINORs required.

No implementation code added -- verified by grep for elixir/ex fenced code blocks after all edits (none found). No lib/ or test/ file touched by this rework (test/support/tenant_template.ex and tenant_fixture.ex remain ELIXIR-DEV's, untouched), only the design doc. This handoff file's existence on disk was verified via a follow-up read after writing it.
result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR for re-validation (Step 2b, rework 3, final in budget), then back to ELIXIR-DEV to add the trigger-recreation step to clone_tenant_schema!/1 and re-verify dimension #8 passes non-vacuously on a real clone.
